Trend

Your 7-day change shows once your log is a week old.

10-day averageDaily weigh-inForecastGoalNoteWeekend

The forecast carries on your weekly trend from the 10-day average on your last weigh-in. The shaded band is the likely range: if the trend holds, the average lands inside it 8 times in 10, given how much your weigh-ins swing from day to day. It can’t foresee a change in what you eat or do, and it looks at most 12 weeks ahead, because weight change usually slows over months.

On a day with a weigh-in, the line averages the weigh-ins from that day and the 9 days before it. A day without one keeps the last weigh-in’s average, for up to 9 days, so the line holds flat when weigh-ins stop. It’s dashed there, and where an average rests on fewer than 4 weigh-ins. When there’s room, a thin line joins each weigh-in to that day’s average, to show how far the day strayed from it. Each change compares the average on your last weigh-in with the one 7, 30 or 90 days before it, or with your first weigh-in for all time.

Monthly summary

    Your monthly summary will appear here after your first weigh-in.

    Each month starts with the 10-day average as it began and ends with the average on its last weigh-in, so it picks up where the month before ended. When an average comes from a weigh-in on another day, as when a month’s last weigh-in comes before its last day or the log starts partway through a month, a date shows which day. The weekly trend is as it stood on the month’s last weigh-in, and milestones show in the month your average first reached them. ~ marks a weekly trend that isn’t clear yet: the weigh-ins so far can’t tell it apart from day-to-day swings.

    Body fat

    You can track your waist too.

    DateWaist10-day average10-day avg.Body fatEdit measurement

    An estimate from the U.S. Army’s one-site tape formula, using your waist at the navel and your 10-day average on the day you measured. A tape estimate can be several points off a lab scan, so it’s most useful for following your own trend.

    What Baseline keeps about you, where it’s kept and who handles it, and how to import weigh-ins, download your data or delete it. The health data privacy policy has the details.

    What Baseline stores

    Your log
    Weigh-ins and their notes, waist measurements and the body fat formula you chose, your height and goal, your units and what the overview shows, and your reminder time and time zone. For weigh-ins you import, which app they came from, and when you imported them. In Baseline’s database at Neon, in the United States, until you delete it.
    Files you import
    Read on your device. Only the weigh-ins in them, with their dates and notes, are sent to Baseline. The file itself never is.
    Reminder devices
    A push address for each device you turn reminders on from, in the same database, until you turn reminders off.
    Your agreement
    Which version of the health data policy you agreed to, and when, in the same database.
    Your account
    Your email address, your name and picture if you sign in with Google, and a record of your sign-ins, such as the browser and IP address. Kept by Clerk, which runs sign-in. None of your log goes to Clerk.
    On this device
    A copy of your log and any changes waiting to sync, so Baseline opens offline. Signing out removes them. A link that fills in a weigh-in waits in its tab until you sign in.

    What Baseline never does

    • No analytics, ads or trackers. The only code on Baseline’s pages that isn’t its own is Clerk’s sign-in, which can add a bot check from Cloudflare when you sign up.
    • No location. The time zone saved with a reminder is the only clue to where you are.
    • Your data is never sold or used for ads, and goes to no one but the services below.

    Who handles it

    Vercel
    Runs Baseline’s site and server. Its logs record each request’s IP address, and the kind of any error the server hits, never your data. They’re kept for up to a day.
    Neon
    Hosts the database, in the United States. Deleted data stays in its restore history for up to 6 hours.
    Clerk
    Runs sign-in and keeps your account.
    Push services
    Apple, Google, Microsoft or Mozilla, depending on your browser, deliver reminders if you turn them on. Each reminder is encrypted, so they can’t read it.

    Your agreement

    To the health data privacy policy of . Withdrawing your agreement deletes your log, as Delete my data does, and Baseline asks again before it saves anything new.

        Delete your data?

        This permanently deletes everything in your log, on every device:

        • Your weigh-ins and their notes
        • Your waist measurements and the body fat formula you chose
        • Your goal and your height
        • Your settings, which go back to kg and cm, with BMI and body fat shown
        • Your reminders, which stop on every device
        • Your agreement to the health data policy, so Baseline asks again before it saves anything new
